THE FULL BREAKDOWN

A deposit is the total.
We’ll show the detail.

Amazon combines sales with refunds, marketplace fees, adjustments and reserve movements. The planned settlement view brings those components together so you can see how the payout was calculated.

Review the accounting categories before posting. Your Xero records should explain the activity, not just repeat the deposit amount.

BUILT AROUND REVIEW

From settlement to Xero.

Account and tax mappings depend on your business. The intended workflow keeps those decisions visible.

  1. 01

    Import

    Bring in available settlement data from your authorised Amazon account.

  2. 02

    Map

    Assign sales, fees, refunds and other categories to the appropriate Xero accounts.

  3. 03

    Review & post

    Check the breakdown and resolve missing information before sending entries.

  4. 04

    Match

    Use the prepared entries to match the corresponding bank deposit in Xero.

BEYOND THE HAPPY PATH

When something needs attention,
you should know why.

Data readiness

Waiting on a report?

We plan to distinguish missing reports and tax data from entries that are ready to review, so you can understand the next step.

Reporting periods

Two months. One payout.

Month-end activity and bank payout dates can differ. Period-aware reporting is part of the planned reconciliation scope.

Cash movements

Held doesn’t mean lost.

Reserve movements affect cash available for payout. They need to be visible separately from the sales and costs behind profitability.

A precise promise.

Reconcile Ready is in development. We plan to help prepare and review accounting entries; final bank matching happens in Xero. Regional tax support, multi-currency handling and automatic posting options will be confirmed before launch.

ACCOUNTS THAT MAKE SENSE

From transaction type
to accounting category.

The planned setup will let you review how Amazon activity maps to your Xero chart of accounts. The right mappings depend on your business.

Example mapping structure — not tax or accounting advice
ActivityWhat it representsIllustrative destination
Sales & refundsProduct revenue and sales reversalsSales and sales returns
Marketplace feesReferral, fulfilment and other Amazon chargesRelevant expense accounts
Reserve movementsMoney Amazon holds or releasesA balance-sheet control account
Tax amountsTax collected or reflected in source reportsTreatment confirmed with your accountant
Other adjustmentsCorrections, reimbursements or other movementsA reviewed category appropriate to the transaction

These are category examples, not prescribed account codes. The product will need complete mappings before it can produce usable entries.

TIMING & CONTROL

A payout period isn’t
always a reporting month.

Sales activity, report availability and bank arrival dates can follow different calendars. We’re designing the review flow to make those differences understandable.

28 SEPTEMBER

Trading activity begins

Sales and fees belong to their relevant reporting period.

30 SEPTEMBER

Month-end boundary

Activity may need to be separated for monthly reporting.

11 OCTOBER

Settlement closes

The payout combines the relevant cash movements.

Illustrative timeline

Period-aware summaries and reserve movements must preserve the relationship to the overall payout. The final posting approach will be confirmed as the integration is developed.

THE NEXT ACTION, EXPLAINED

Know what needs attention.

These example statuses show how we intend to distinguish data readiness from posting and bank matching.

Waiting for data

A source report is not ready yet.

Show which report is missing and when it was last checked. A bank deposit alone does not establish that all underlying data is available.

Needs review

A mapping or total needs checking.

Surface missing categories or a difference in the settlement total. The review should explain the issue rather than silently force a balance.

Ready to post

The prepared entry is ready for review.

Inspect the breakdown and selected accounts before sending it to Xero. This status does not mean the bank deposit has been matched.

Posted to Xero

The accounting entry has been sent.

Keep a reference to the destination entry. The bank match is a separate step, completed in Xero.
